Commercial analytics · Creative operations

From inquiry to order.

A SQL analysis of which industrial buyers were most likely to place an order.

Role

Senior Marketing & Brand Consultant

Period

2024–Present

Scope

Eight-person team · Canada, the U.S. and Dubai

01

Executive Summary

For an industrial-parts supplier, I used SQL to trace inquiries to orders and compared conversion by segment and source. I recommended focusing on maintenance teams and tightening lead qualification. During the pilot, 26% of qualified leads became orders, up from 20%. In separate creative work, I standardized briefs and reviews across an eight-person team. Revision cycles fell by 40%.

02

The Challenge

The industrial supplier needed to decide which inquiries deserved sales follow-up. Across our agency accounts, the team also needed a clearer way to brief and approve creative work.

03

The Execution

  1. Trace the sales funnel

    Compared customer, opportunity and order data in SQL to identify where qualified inquiries became orders.

  2. Set the commercial direction

    Partnered with senior executives on positioning, messaging, go-to-market plans and campaign KPIs.

  3. Lead the team

    Led an eight-person team supporting marketing and client engagements across three markets.

  4. Improve creative operations

    Standardized brand kits, review workflows and quality assurance.

  5. Connect delivery with reporting

    Brought demand-generation activity and analytics into client reviews.

04

The Impact

20% → 26%Qualified leads that became orders during the pilot
−40%Creative revision cycles across the team
